title: Finite averaging and topological invariant summands in internal condensed modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$ let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], on the small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the categories $\mathcal A_P(C_F)$ of internal $C_F$-modules with linear condensed $P$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For a finite group $Q$ with its discrete topology and a profinite group $L$, write $M^Q$ for sections fixed after every profinite base change by every generalized element of $Q$, retaining the $L$-action.

Suppose $m=|Q|$ is prime to $\ell$. For each $M\in\mathcal A_{Q\times L}(C_F)$ the internal $L$-equivariant endomorphism
$$e_M=m^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q}q$$
is idempotent, has image $M^Q$, and is the identity on $M^Q$. The scalar $m^{-1}$ denotes the constant section in $C_F$. The functor $\Gamma_Q^L:M\mapsto M^Q$ from $\mathcal A_{Q\times L}(C_F)$ to $\mathcal A_L(C_F)$ is exact, including preservation of epimorphisms of internal module sheaves.

Let $W$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with a continuous $E$-linear $Q\times L$-action. Give $W^Q$ its subspace topology and residual $L$-action. Write $W_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E W)$ and $(W^Q)_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E W^Q)$, with finite-dimensional product norm topologies [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation]. The average $e_W=m^{-1}\sum_q\rho(q)$ has image $W^Q$ and supplies a continuous $L$-equivariant splitting. The scalar-extended inclusion induces a homeomorphism onto the invariant subspace
$$F\otimes_E W^Q\xrightarrow{\sim}(F\otimes_E W)^Q$$
and an isomorphism of internal $C_F$-modules with residual $L$-action
$$\theta_F:(W^Q)_F\xrightarrow{\sim}(W_F)^Q.$$
This is the map induced by the actual invariant inclusion, natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps of $W$. Under the coefficient morphism $C_E\to C_\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the two identifications commute with $w\mapsto1\otimes w$; explicitly $e_\Omega(1\otimes w)=1\otimes e_E(w)$. The zero representation, zero invariant subspace, trivial $Q$ or $L$, and the empty profinite test set are included. No completeness of $\Omega$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $R=C_F$. The definition [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] already supplies the section modules, restriction maps and section-natural linear actions on each internal module. Thus its objects and morphisms give exactly the sheaf-action data of [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation], with $K=\underline{Q\times L}$ or $K=\underline L$; no new comparison of internal and sectionwise modules is needed here. These are sheaves of groups: continuous maps glue along jointly surjective finite profinite covers, and multiplication and inversion are pointwise. Apply that theorem: the two action categories are abelian, their kernels are sectionwise kernels, and forgetting actions creates kernels and cokernels and detects exactness. The site is small under [def-weil-size-convention]; its finite limits are products and closed equalizers of profinite sets. The commutative ring sheaf is supplied by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], applied to the topological field $F$. All groups, finite limits and coefficient values are within the fixed universe bound.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: sectionwise interpretation and abelian action categories

proof.text: Since $m=|Q|\geq1$ and $F$ contains the characteristic-zero field $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], the constant section $1/m$ is an inverse to $m$ in every $R(S)$. The prime-to-$\ell$ assumption in particular suffices. For $x\in M(S)$ define $e_Sx=m^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q}(q,1)x$. Naturality of the action makes these linear maps commute with restriction. For each constant $a\in Q$, reindexing the finite sums by $q\mapsto aq$ and $q\mapsto qa$ gives $a e_S=e_S=e_S a$. Every generalized $l\in C(S,L)$ commutes with every $(q,1)$, so $e_S$ commutes with the residual $L$-action. If all constant $q$ fix $x$, then $e_Sx=m^{-1}mx=x$. These are finite-sum identities, valid also at the empty test object.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: the finite-sum identities

proof.text: Constant-$Q$ fixed sections are fully fixed in the internal sense. Indeed, given $T\to S$ and $g:T\to Q$ continuous, the finitely many clopen profinite subsets $T_q=g^{-1}(q)$ form a finite jointly surjective family, hence a cover in the coherent profinite topology (empty fibres may be omitted). On $T_q$, the action of $g$ is the action of the constant $q$, so $g\cdot x|_T=x|_T$ there. Sheaf separatedness gives this equality on $T$. The converse uses $T=S$ and constant $g$. The constant-fixed section submodules form a sheaf: their compatibility equations are preserved by restriction, and gluing in $M$ preserves the equations by separatedness. They are stable under the residual $L$-action. Step 2 therefore gives a map $p_M:M\to M^Q$, with inclusion $i_M:M^Q\to M$, satisfying $i_Mp_M=e_M$ and $p_Mi_M=1$. Consequently $e_M^2=e_M$, its image as a sheaf is exactly $M^Q$, and it acts identically there. Also $p_M$ is $Q\times L$-equivariant if its target is given trivial $Q$-action: the identity $e_Sa=e_S$ extends from constant $a$ to generalized $a$ by the same clopen cover.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: generalized elements and the split invariant submodule

proof.text: For an equivariant $f:M\to N$, restrict $f$ to fixed sections to define $\Gamma f:M^Q\to N^Q$. It is linear and $L$-equivariant; it preserves identities, composition and sums. The formula for the average gives $f e_M=e_N f$, hence $p_Nf=(\Gamma f)p_M$ and $f i_M=i_N(\Gamma f)$. Kernels are sectionwise by [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation]. Thus, if $K=\ker f$, the sections of $K^Q$ are precisely the fully fixed $x\in M(S)$ with $f(x)=0$, which are also the sections of $\ker(\Gamma f)$. This identifies $\Gamma K$ with that kernel over $M^Q$. The zero object is preserved as well.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: functoriality, natural retractions and kernels

proof.text: Let $f:M\to N$ be epic in the action category. If $a,b:N^Q\to T$ are $L$-equivariant maps with $a\Gamma f=b\Gamma f$, then $(a p_N)f=a(\Gamma f)p_M=b(\Gamma f)p_M=(b p_N)f$. The composites $a p_N,b p_N$ are $Q\times L$-equivariant maps to $T$ with trivial $Q$-action, by step 3. Cancellation of the epimorphism $f$ gives $a p_N=b p_N$, and composition with $i_N$ gives $a=b$. Therefore $\Gamma f$ is epic. The identical cancellation argument with arbitrary internal-module maps $a,b$ proves more: whenever the underlying internal-module map $f$ is epic, the underlying map $\Gamma f$ is epic. This uses the definition of an epimorphism and the actual retraction $p_Ni_N=1$; it makes no assertion that $f(S)$ is surjective.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: epimorphisms, including epimorphisms of internal module sheaves

proof.text: Consider any exact complex $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}C$ in the source abelian category. Write $k:K\to B$ for the kernel of $v$ and $u':A\to K$ for the factorization of $u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-iff-epi-kernel-lift], $u'$ is epic. Step 4 identifies $\Gamma k$ with the kernel of $\Gamma v$, and step 5 makes $\Gamma u'$ epic. Apply the same cited criterion in the target abelian category to conclude exactness at $\Gamma B$. Both categories are abelian by [lem-sfb-sheaf-action-grothendieck-inflation]. Together with additivity this proves that $\Gamma_Q^L$ is exact, not merely left exact.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: exactness from the kernel criterion

proof.text: For the actual continuous representation $W$, the same finite-sum calculation gives $e_W(W)=W^Q$, $e_W|_{W^Q}=1$ and $e_W\rho(l)=\rho(l)e_W$. The map $e_W$ is continuous: each fixed $\rho(q)$ is continuous by the given action, and addition and multiplication by the fixed scalar $1/m$ are continuous. Its corestriction $p:W\to W^Q$ is continuous for the subspace topology, as is the inclusion $i:W^Q\to W$. They are $L$-equivariant, $pi=1$ and $ip=e_W$. The restricted $L$-action on $W^Q$ is jointly continuous since its inclusion into $W$ is, and it lands in that subspace. This is the claimed topological splitting, with the actual invariant inclusion of [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: continuous splitting before scalar extension

proof.text: The image $W^Q=p(W)$ is finite-dimensional: if $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ span $W$, their images $p(b_j)$ span it. The field $E$ is complete by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] and nontrivially normed since $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}\ne1$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Both $W$ and the subspace $W^Q$ are Hausdorff topological $E$-vector spaces. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism] to their coordinate linear equivalences with finite powers of $E$. Thus their given topologies are the finite-dimensional product topologies used in [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation]. After tensoring with $F$, choose the extended bases. A matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ for an $E$-linear map then acts by $y_i=\sum_j a_{ij}x_j$ on finite powers of $F$. Each coordinate is continuous by finite addition and scalar multiplication in $F$, so its tensor extension is continuous. This also shows basis independence, since the inverse change-of-basis matrix has the same property. For the group action, its matrix entries are continuous functions of the group element (evaluate the continuous action on each basis vector, then take continuous coordinates). Embedding those entries into $F$ gives a jointly continuous extended action. This applies to $W$ and $W^Q$ and invokes completeness only for $E$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: the product topologies and continuous scalar-extended maps

proof.text: Put $I_F=1\otimes i$ and $P_F=1\otimes p$ on the actual tensor-product modules. On pure tensors, $P_F I_F=1$ and $I_F P_F=1\otimes e_W=e_F$, where $e_F=m^{-1}\sum_q(1\otimes\rho(q))$; pure tensors generate, so these identities hold everywhere. The maps are continuous by step 8 and $L$-equivariant by their formulas. The calculation of step 2 for the ordinary $F$-representation shows $e_Fz$ is fixed by all $q$, and $e_Fz=z$ for fixed $z$. For $u\in F\otimes_EW^Q$, the splitting identities give $e_F I_Fu=I_F P_F I_Fu=I_Fu$, so $I_Fu$ is fixed. For fixed $z$, they give $I_F P_Fz=e_Fz=z$; conversely $P_F I_Fu=u$. Thus $I_F$ lands in $(F\otimes_EW)^Q$, and $I_F$ and the restriction of $P_F$ are mutually inverse there. Corestricting $I_F$ to that invariant subspace and restricting $P_F$ preserve continuity for the subspace topology. Thus the actual inclusion induces the asserted homeomorphism $F\otimes_EW^Q\simeq(F\otimes_EW)^Q$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: tensoring the splitting and identifying the invariant subspace

proof.text: For a profinite $S$, a section $v:S\to F\otimes_EW$ is internally fixed precisely when its values lie in $(F\otimes_EW)^Q$. One direction follows by taking constant $q$ and evaluating; the other follows directly from $(g\cdot v)(t)=\rho(g(t))v(t)$ after any $T\to S$. A continuous map with values in a subspace corestricts continuously to that subspace by the definition of its topology. Therefore postcomposition by $I_F$ gives a bijection from $C(S,F\otimes_EW^Q)$ to the fully fixed sections, with inverse postcomposition by $P_F$. These bijections are pointwise $C(S,F)$-linear, commute with restrictions and are $C(S,L)$-equivariant. By the section identifications and morphism specification of [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation], they form the isomorphism $\theta_F$ of internal modules with residual $L$-action, induced by the actual inclusion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: identification of all continuous invariant sections

proof.text:
If $f:W\to W'$ is a continuous equivariant $E$-linear map, the finite sums give $f e_W=e_{W'}f$. For $w\in W^Q$ its restriction satisfies $f(w)\in(W')^Q$, and the inclusion square $f i=i'f|_{W^Q}$ commutes. Consequently $(1\otimes f)I_F=I'_F(1\otimes f|_{W^Q})$ on every pure tensor and hence everywhere. Postcomposition on $S$ gives naturality of $\theta_F$; the inverse maps commute as well by $p'f=f|_{W^Q}p$. For coefficients, under the identification $E\otimes_EW\simeq W$, calculate
$$e_\Omega(1\otimes w)=m^{-1}\sum_q1\otimes\rho(q)w=1\otimes\left(m^{-1}\sum_q\rho(q)w\right)=1\otimes e_W(w).$$
Likewise $I_\Omega(1\otimes u)=1\otimes i(u)$ and $P_\Omega(1\otimes w)=1\otimes p(w)$. These equalities prove the coefficient squares for both the vector-space identifications and their section maps. The latter are maps over the postcomposition morphism $C_E\to C_\Omega$ of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], exactly as specified by [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of finite averaging: naturality and the explicit coefficient identity

proof.text: If $Q=1$, then $m=1$ and $e,p,i$ are identities; if $L=1$, the same formulas simply have no residual equivariance condition. If $W=0$ or $W^Q=0$, the maps to or from that space are the unique zero maps and all the displayed splitting and tensor identities still hold. At $S=\varnothing$, continuous-section modules are zero modules and all equalities hold for their unique sections; for arbitrary internal modules the sheaf axiom for the empty covering likewise gives the unique section. Every average and every matrix formula is finite. No integral, convergent series, completion of $\Omega$ or completeness assertion about $\Omega$ occurs.
